AnchorPack.description:
A surveyed anchor map for one circuit.

Shipped beside the circuit pack rather than inside it because it decays on a different clock: the geography is good for a decade, the Wi-Fi estate is re-cabled between events.

surveyed_at.description: when the survey was walked, ISO 8601. A fix from a year-old anchor map is a guess wearing a number.

Availability.description:
When an edge exists at all (D5).

`blocked: bool` cannot express "open until quali, then closed for sixty minutes". At-grade crossings close whenever cars are running, which makes routing time-dependent: a path is valid only if each edge is still open when the walker would actually reach it.

close_lead_s.description: closes this long before cars run

CircuitPack.description: One venue. Swapping circuits must require no code change.

Confidence.description:
How much to trust the state beside it.

Never presented without the claim it qualifies. With thirty nodes reporting, the system says so; it does not quietly present the same number it would give for four hundred.

reportable.description: The contract's served judgement; clients never restate its thresholds.

stability.description: agreement with recent estimates for this zone

CoordinateFrame.description: Local metric frame. Derived from the source bbox, never estimated.

venue_bounds_m.description: (min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y). Larger than the track: car parks, campsites and park-and-ride sit outside it. Sizing to the track clips arrival routes.

Crossing.description:
The dominant bottleneck mechanism at a circuit.

Bridges and tunnels stay open but carry far less than the at-grade crossings they replace — which is exactly why they pinch when a session starts.

CrossingClosed.description: Authored CrowdFlow wire contracts. Runtime derivations live beside them.

opens_at.description: absolute unix seconds; None when no reopening time is known

CrossingNotice.description: A timetable fact a spectator cannot infer by looking at the crossing.

closes_at.description: absolute unix seconds; None when no closing time is known

CrowdNode.description:
One anonymous device's live movement state.

node_id is a rotating pseudonym, not an identity. It is valid only within its rotation epoch and must never be joined across epochs.

epoch.description: ID rotation epoch; IDs are not comparable across epochs

node_id.description: rotating pseudonym, valid within its epoch only

zone_id.description: assigned by the state engine, not self-reported

Edge.description:
A walkable connection.

width_m matters more than it looks: flow rate is per metre of width, so the LOS band cannot be computed without it.

capacity_flow_ped_m_min.description: observed peak sustained flow per metre of width; never invented

free_speed_ms.description: observed where available, else the standards prior

gradient.description: rise over run; affects walking speed

width_m.description: required — LOS flow is per metre of width

EventProfile.description:
This weekend's timetable. Changes every event; the circuit does not.

The chequered flag is the largest crowd-movement trigger of the day, so this feeds the predictor directly, not just the display.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, where the source gives one. For a flag, nothing more.

date.description: Race day, ISO 8601 date. The weekend spans three days; this is the one that matters, and the one the chequered-flag egress trigger hangs off.

locality.description: Town, then country. How a venue is found on a map and named in a ticket.

round.description: Championship round. What a spectator actually says — "round twelve", not a circuit id — and the natural sort key for a season.

utc_offset.description:
The venue's offset from UTC over the weekend, as '+01:00'.

Carried because every timestamp in this contract is UTC and every session time a spectator reads is local. A phone at the circuit is on venue time anyway; a phone being used to plan the trip from another country is not, and that is exactly when somebody misreads a start time by an hour.

Forecast.description:
Where congestion will be, when, and why.

The headline is time_to_threshold_s, not the current value. "2:47 until capacity" drives a decision; "87% full" does not.

actionable.description: Served judgement: clients must not duplicate these thresholds.

horizon_s.description: how far ahead this forecast looks

model_id.description: which model produced this; baseline is a valid answer

projected_peak_density_persons_m2.description: persons/m2 at the projected peak; bands are classified on density

target_band.description: the band predicted to be crossed

time_to_threshold_s.description: None when the threshold is not projected to be crossed

IngestAck.description: The server's answer to a batch.

server_time.description: unix seconds, server clock. Lets a handset correct drift without a time API — timestamps decide the staleness window, so a phone six minutes fast reports nothing that counts.

stop.description: Stop uploading and stop sensing. Set when the session has ended or the disclosure this report cites is no longer served. A phone that keeps sensing after the event is a battery complaint and a privacy problem.

InterventionCandidate.description: One simulated what-if. Rejected candidates are kept and displayed.

description.description: plain language, e.g. 'Divert 30% of Vale to Gate 4'

projected_walk_time_delta_s.description: positive means longer. Always shown beside the benefit, never hidden.

recommendation_note.description: engine-authored reason this option is recommended; absent otherwise

LinkStatus.description: Freshness and reachability, stated rather than hidden.

updated_at.description: unix seconds of the newest observation behind the route

MeshMessage.description:
Envelope for anything crossing the mesh.

sequence prevents duplicate processing; ttl stops packets travelling forever. Both are enforced at every hop, not just at the destination.

source.description: rotating node pseudonym of the originator

NodeReport.description:
What a handset uploads.

Deliberately made of CrowdNode and nothing else. There are no anchor ids here, no RSSI, no scan lists: those are resolved on the phone and dropped. A report is a position, a speed and a heading under a rotating pseudonym — enough to count a crowd, not enough to follow a person.

Batched because uplinks are opportunistic (D7): a phone with no data connection keeps sensing and sends the backlog when it next has one.

consent_version.description: which disclosure this person actually agreed to. A report under an unknown consent version is rejected, not accepted-and-flagged.

node_id.description: rotating pseudonym, valid within its epoch only

nodes.description: one or more samples, oldest first

sources.description: which radios were usable while this batch was formed. Explains a coverage gap: 'the zone is empty' and 'every phone in the zone lost its anchor map' look identical without it.

Position.description:
A point in the venue's local metric frame, in metres.

Never latitude/longitude. Lat/lon exists only at the circuit pack's origin and at the device's location adapter (plan.md section 10).

PositionFix.description:
A resolved position, with the honesty attached.

`accuracy_m` is a one-sigma radius, and `residual_m` is what the solve could not explain. They fail apart on purpose: a tight `accuracy_m` beside a large `residual_m` means the anchor map is wrong, not that the phone is confused, and that is the difference between recalibrating a venue and blaming a handset.

accuracy_m.description: positional one-sigma. Feeds Confidence; never zero.

anchors_used.description: anchors that contributed. Zero for GNSS, and a two-anchor fix is a weighted centroid rather than a trilateration — the count is how a reader tells which.

heading_deg.description: degrees clockwise from north. Null when speed is below the noise floor, because the heading of a stationary phone is noise with a number on it.

residual_m.description: RMS of the range residuals, metres. Null when the source does not solve (GNSS).

speed_ms.description: metres per second, from successive fixes. Null until there are two.

RadioAnchor.description:
One surveyed radio landmark at a known place in the venue.

`anchor_id` is a digest of the hardware identifier (BSSID, or beacon UUID/major/minor), never the identifier itself. That is not a privacy measure — the MAC space is small enough to brute force — it is so that a pack committed to this repository does not publish a venue's Wi-Fi infrastructure inventory. The privacy measure is that anchor ids stay on the handset.

`rssi_at_1m_dbm` and `path_loss_exponent` are per-anchor because they are properties of an installation, not of a radio standard: an AP behind a metal panel and one on a mast have the same chipset and different curves. Both are Sourced, so a pack can be honest that a given anchor was placed off a site plan (assumed) rather than walked (measured), and the solver can down-weight it accordingly.

anchor_id.description: digest of the hardware identifier, never the identifier

floor.description: for multi-level venues; null in a single-level frame

path_loss_exponent.description: the exponent of the log-distance model. Free space is 2; a packed concourse is nearer 3.5 because bodies absorb 2.4 GHz.

rssi_at_1m_dbm.description: calibrated received strength at one metre — the intercept of the range curve

RadioObservation.description: One radio heard once. Never leaves the handset except in an operator survey.

frequency_mhz.description: 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz attenuate differently; the solver uses it to pick the exponent when the anchor does not supply one

rssi_dbm.description: received signal strength, dBm. Negative; closer to zero is stronger.

RerouteCommand.description:
What actually goes over the mesh.

Deliberately NOT a per-person route. Broadcasting avoid/prefer sets and letting each device compute its own path scales, and works offline (plan.md section 33).

expected_cost_s.description: honest added walking time, stated before the user accepts

expires_at.description: commands must expire; stale routing is harmful

reason.description: plain language, surfaced in the app

target_fraction.description: share of affected walkers this should reach

RerouteOffer.description: A proposed alternative and the safety verdict that gates its display.

Route.description: Where the spectator is, where they are going and the walk between them.

total_walk_s.description: door-to-door seconds from routing, including waits; never summed on the phone

SafetyConstraints.description: Hard rules the agent cannot override.

SafetyVerdict.description:
The gate every action passes through.

Hard constraints the AI cannot override: never route through a blocked or forbidden edge, never intentionally exceed capacity, never route away from emergency exits during evacuation (plan.md section 34).

dispatchable.description:
Only the exact command reviewed as APPROVED may leave the gate.

``MODIFIED`` describes a rejected proposal for which safety can suggest a correction; it does not contain that corrected command. Dispatching the original in that state would act on the version safety changed. A corrected command must be issued separately and reviewed in full.

reason.description: stated even on approval; rejections are explained

ScoreBreakdown.description:
Why a candidate scored what it did.

Shown to the operator. An intervention recommendation without its components is an assertion; with them it is an argument.

SensingStatus.description:
What one handset's sensing stack is doing, as the person is shown it.

Exists as a contract rather than app state because the app must be able to answer "what are you doing with my phone right now" in the same words the console uses. A settings screen that paraphrases is a settings screen that drifts.

active.description: whether the loop is running at all

available.description: radios usable on this handset right now, best first

blocked_by.description: why sensing is not running, in words a person can act on ('Bluetooth is off', not 'ERR_ADAPTER_STATE')

queued.description: samples held because there is no uplink

using.description: the source of the most recent accepted fix

end_provenance.description:
Whether the end time was published or inferred.

Session ends move — a race runs long, a session is red-flagged — and the egress prediction hangs off the end of the race more than anything else in this system. An assumed end is a guess about the largest crowd-movement trigger of the day, and it must not read like a schedule.

kind.description: practice | qualifying | sprint | race | support | ceremony

name.description: As the sport names it: 'Practice 1', 'Sprint Qualifying', 'Race'.

Sourced.description: A value with its provenance and, where applicable, its sample count.

SpectatorView.description: One of the six screen states for a race day.

Step.description: One already-priced leg of a route.

to.description: human-readable landmark from the circuit pack

walk_s.description: walking seconds computed by the routing engine

SurveyReport.description:
An operator walk test: observations WITH their positions, to build an anchor map.

The one path where raw radio observations legitimately leave a device, and it is a staff device on a surveying job, not a spectator's phone. Separate contract, separate endpoint, separate consent — so that no amount of refactoring can quietly widen the spectator path into this one.

surveyor.description: who walked it; a staff identifier, not a pseudonym

accuracy_m.description: how well the surveyor knew where they were standing

position.description: ground truth for this sample, venue frame

TraceFragment.description:
A short, noised path segment contributed for venue refinement.

Carries planar Laplace noise applied ON DEVICE before storage (geo-indistinguishability, Andres et al. CCS 2013 -- see plan/methods.md section 4). Fragments are deliberately too short to reconstruct one person's day, and their IDs rotate per fragment.

Accurate in aggregate, deniable individually: map refinement is density estimation over many fragments, and zero-mean noise averages out.

fragment_id.description: per-fragment random; never reused, never linkable

noise_radius_m.description: radius within which the true path is indistinguishable

VenueState.description: Every zone at one tick, plus what the system knows it cannot see.

unobserved_zones.description: Zones with no reporting device. MUST render as unknown, never as empty. Under D7 uplinks are opportunistic, so coverage genuinely varies.

Zone.description: A named place. Imported from OSM tags where possible.

band.description:
Operational band, classified on density (see standards.band_for_density).

CRITICAL means at or beyond capacity density — the point where flow stops improving and starts to collapse — not a high flow number.

density_persons_m2.description: persons per square metre — the AUTHORITATIVE measure. Flow is not monotonic in density (it peaks then collapses), so a band cannot be read off flow alone: a jammed corridor and an empty one look alike.

estimated_population.description:
Observed devices scaled by measured participation.

The single most load-bearing number in the system, which is why participation_rate is measured rather than configured.

flow_ped_m_min.description: pedestrians per metre width per minute — reported, not classified on

los_grade.description: Full Fruin grade A-F. Console only; the app never shows this.

net_flow_per_min.description: Positive means filling. Sustained positive net flow is the early warning.

over_capacity.description: Past the peak of the fundamental diagram: more arrivals now reduce throughput. The single most important operator signal.

queue_excess.description: people who do not fit at jam density, i.e. backed up behind
